problem: Whether the variance alone forces a universal lower bound V·δ_k ≥ κ on the normalized Turán deficit δ_k = 1 − f_{k−1}f_{k+1}/f_k^2 near the mode of every Poisson–binomial law with V ≥ 1.
debate: The literature on how much slack log-concavity and ultra-log-concavity leave in Bernoulli-sum pmfs (Hillion–Johnson, Johnson, Dümbgen–Wellner), alongside mode-location and maximal-mass results (Darroch, Pitman, Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne).
gap: Existing lower bounds on δ_k are scaled by n, by the success probabilities, or by k rather than by V, and they all degenerate near the mode when summands with p_i near 0 and near 1 pile up at fixed variance; the mode-location and maximal-mass results give no lower bound on δ_k at all.
contribution: A proof that V·δ_D ≥ 1/4 at the first-descent index, a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3, consequent bounds δ_k ≥ 1/(4V+|k−D|) everywhere and 1/(4V+1) ≤ δ_c < 2/V at the rightmost mode, and a Haar-unitary eigenvalue-count example where the bound improves from order 1/N to order 1/log N, with the key one-variable inequality checked in exact arithmetic by Bernstein expansions.
note: The theorem is clean, in scope and well posed, but the opening justifies a variance-scaled bound on the Turán deficit only with a Gaussian heuristic and one unitary-matrix example and never says what it is needed for, so expect referees to press on that, on the open 1/4 to 1/3 gap, and on the computer-assisted step.
